title: The Quran: Surah 99, az-Zalzalah (The Quake)
author: Tradução inglesa de Talal Itani (ClearQuran)
tradition: Texto sagrado do Islão, século VII
intro: Lição sobre a Surata 99. O texto inglês é a tradução de Talal Itani, reproduzida sem alterações; as notas de língua, perguntas, discussão e escrita são material pedagógico separado, baseado apenas no que o próprio texto diz.

source.title: Quran English Translation: Clear, Pure, Easy to Read Modern English
source.edition: Edition A (uses the word 'Allah' to refer to the Creator)

questions.q: What will the earth bring out, according to verse 2?
questions.why: O versículo 2 diz: 'the earth brings out its loads'.
'In droves' quer dizer em grande número.

questions.q: Verse 6 says people will emerge 'to be shown their works'. What does this suggest?
options: That what people have done will be shown to them
That people will forget what they did
That people will build something new
questions.why: O texto diz 'to be shown their works'.

questions.q: Which two verses are almost the same, except for one word?
questions.why: Os versículos 7 e 8 só trocam 'good' por 'evil' e juntam 'And'.

questions.q: Which sentence best sums up verses 7 and 8?
options: Only large actions will be seen
Even the smallest good or evil will be seen
questions.why: 'An atom's weight' é uma medida muito pequena, e os dois versículos acabam com 'will see it'.

B2.discussion: Verses 7 and 8 use a very small weight to talk about what people do. Why might a text choose such a small measure?
B2.writing: Write 80 to 100 words: Say what happens to the earth and to the people in this passage.

questions.q: What does man say in verse 3?
options: What is the matter with it?
questions.why: O versículo 3 diz: 'And man says, “What is the matter with it?”'

questions.q: In 'Whoever has done an atom's weight of good will see it', 'whoever' means:
Verse 4 says the earth 'will tell its tales' and verse 5 says 'your Lord will have inspired it'. What explanation do the two verses give together?
options: The earth speaks because man asked
The earth speaks because it was inspired
questions.why: O versículo 5 começa com 'For' e dá a razão do versículo 4.

questions.q: How does 'And whoever...' in verse 8 relate to 'Whoever...' in verse 7?
options: It is a parallel sentence that gives the opposite case
questions.why: O versículo 7 fala do bem e o 8 fala do mal, com a mesma construção.

questions.q: Which description of the passage is best supported?
options: A shaking earth (1 and 2), a human question (3), the earth telling (4 and 5), people shown their works (6), and two parallel results (7 and 8)
questions.why: Cada grupo de versículos tem uma função clara.

C1.discussion: The passage moves from a physical event, the earth shaking, to what it means for people. How does this order shape the reader's attention?
C1.writing: Write 120 to 150 words: Explain how verses 7 and 8 work as a pair.

glossary: o peso de um átomo de mal

questions.q: In which verse does 'On that Day' appear for the first time?
questions.why: 'On that Day' aparece pela primeira vez no versículo 4 e volta no versículo 6.

questions.q: 'The earth brings out its loads' and 'it will tell its tales' show the earth as:
options: an agent that acts and speaks
questions.why: Os verbos 'brings out' e 'tell' têm a terra como sujeito.

questions.q: In verse 3, man asks 'What is the matter with it?' and verse 4 answers. What does the answer make clear?
options: That the earth itself will give the explanation
That man will give the explanation
That the question is a mistake
questions.why: O versículo 4 diz 'it will tell its tales'.

questions.q: Verses 7 and 8 differ only in 'good' and 'evil' (and the opening 'And'). What effect does this near repetition have?
options: It sets two opposites side by side with the same weight and the same result
questions.why: As duas frases têm a mesma medida e o mesmo fim, 'will see it'.

questions.q: Which statement is best supported by the passage as a whole?
options: It moves from a physical event to its meaning for people, and ends with two parallel results
It tells one story with one character
questions.why: Versículos 1 e 2: acontecimento físico. Versículos 3 a 6: o que isso significa para as pessoas. Versículos 7 e 8: resultados paralelos.

C2.discussion: The passage opens with a loud physical event and closes with the smallest possible measure. What does this movement from huge to tiny do?
C2.writing: Write 150 to 200 words: Analyse how the eight verses move from the earth to the people, referring to specific words and to the pair in verses 7 and 8.
